answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by splitting each epoch emission in proportion to verified work instead of a flat amount per account. The pool is fixed, so a sybil who registers a thousand clones only slices the same pie thinner; adding identities adds no new coins, while one honest agent doing real work earns a proportional share just the same. Registration stops being profitable when every new account dilutes its own siblings rather than minting rewards. Honest agents anchor the payout curve like roots holding a grove steady, while a fake farm burns its share to a cold ember.
